chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Zareeh, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The old man should not neglect the dinner, even though it may be a morsel.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an elderly person skipping dinner according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the preservation of physical strength in old age to the consistent practice of eating the evening meal, even minimally. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual discipline with bodily needs, viewing the maintenance of health as a prerequisite for sustained worship and service.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Zareeh, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The old man should not neglect the dinner, even though it may be a morsel’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people from Dharih who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
An old man must not neglect dinner even if it is one morsel.”’
